title: AIDA playbooks record
description: The plays every role that writes or judges code follows, at <task folder>/records/playbooks.json (ideal/playbooks.md, 'The record'). Written by `playbooks load`, which reads the person's file and the project's file itself and merges the catalog record the playbook-loader agent wrote. records/playbooks.md beside it is rendered from this file and no script parses it back. A field present in a real record but absent from `properties` is a defect in the schema, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field every other record carries. Bumped only when a later change to this schema says so.

loadedAt.description: When `playbooks load` wrote this file, ISO 8601 UTC. Running load again is the repair for a stale record.

sources.description: One entry per source read, in precedence order: person, project, each folder the project declares as a source of playbooks in its own declared order, then each catalog set. The four states are distinct on purpose: a person with no file is `absent`, a set the navigator could not reach is `unreachable`, a file with no plays is `empty`. Only `loaded` with a count is coverage, and review's framework-practices check reads these states for its floor.

plays.description: Every play from every loaded source, in source order. A role follows each play whose `when` covers the files it owns, and a reviewer's finding cites the play's `id`.

source.description: `person`, `project`, the path of a folder the project declares as a source of playbooks, or a set id shaped <framework>/best-practices/<author>.

plays.description: How many plays this source contributed. Zero for every state but loaded.

id.description: <source>:<slug>. The slug is the title lowercased, runs of non-alphanumerics to one hyphen, trimmed; `pb_slug` in scripts/lib/playbooks.sh is the one rule.

source.description: The source this play came from, one of the `sources` entries.

domain.description: The `## <Domain>` heading the play sits under, or the catalog topic.

title.description: The `### <Title>` line: the rule, as a statement.

what.description: The **What:** line. A play with none loads with its title here, and load warned once.

rationale.description: The **Rationale:** line: why, and what breaks without it.

when.description: The **When it applies:** line: file types, contexts, exceptions. A role matches the files it owns against this.

example.description: The fenced block after **Example:**, fences included, verbatim. Empty when the play has none.

guide.description: <topic>/<file>.md for a catalog play, the guide that holds the detail. Null for a play from a file.
